content: The Primary Nursing Assistant Editor-in-Chief, Michelle Lew, is requested to take over this page and consider applying to become the Editor-in-Chief for this topic. It is permissible for there to be one or more Editors-in-Chief for this subject. Additionally, individuals may apply to serve as an Associate Editor-in-Chief for one of the subtopics listed below. Interested candidates are encouraged to contact us to express their interest in serving either as the Editor-in-Chief for the entire topic or as an Associate Editor-in-Chief for a specific subtopic. Applicants should ensure that they attach their CV and/or a biographical sketch when submitting their application. Primary nursing is a model of nursing practice that prioritizes continuity of care by assigning one nurse, often in collaboration with a nursing assistant, to provide comprehensive care for a small group of inpatients within a hospital's nursing unit. The designated primary nurse assumes responsibility for coordinating all aspects of care for the same group of patients throughout their stay in a specific area. This includes tasks such as administering medications, performing treatments, and other related duties.
